page.layout: One page of text, set as a psalm: a heading at the top, then seven verse stanzas in italic. Below the last stanza, at the right, a catchword with a row of asterisks before it. No margin notes, no page number, no running head.

main_text.l: DEus misereatur nostri, & benedi-cat nobis, lucere faciat vultum suum apud nos. Selah.

l.i: Vt cognoscatur in terra via tua, in omnibus gentibus salus tua.
Celebrent te populi ô Deus, celebrent te populi universi.

main_text.l: Gaudeant nationes & ovent, quod jus redditurus sis ex æquitate populis, & nationes in terra deducturus sis. Selah.

l.i: Celebrent te ô Deus populi, celebrent te populi universi.
Terra vero reddat proventum suum, & benedicat nobis Deus, Deus noster.
Benedicat nobis Deus, & metuant eum omnes fines terræ.

page.notes: The initial D is a large woodcut-style letter joined to the word "Eus" as "Deus". Faint show-through of the reverse page is visible in the right half and was not transcribed. The asterisks before the catchword are a printed ornament, not text. The word "Selah" is set in roman type, not italic. The heading is a division (Psalmus) with number LXVII, so caput is 67.
